mainTopic: The שולחן: its status as a wooden vessel, a person's table bringing כפרה, the panels and rods and שבת, and the size of the אמה in the מקדש
overview: The amud begins with רבי יוחנן's rule that a covered wooden vessel always takes the status of its metal covering. That seems to make the gold-covered שולחן a gold vessel. The גמרא answers that the שולחן is different because a פסוק in יחזקאל calls it 'wood'. That פסוק switches from 'מזבח' to 'שולחן'. רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר learn from this that today, without a בית המקדש, a person's table brings כפרה. Next, רב קטינא finds the gold panels and rods of the שולחן in a פסוק in שמות. רבא first challenges this, because handling the rods does not override שבת. He then takes the challenge back, using רבי עקיבא's rule that work which can be done at another time does not override שבת. A ברייתא describes how the rods were taken out before שבת and put back after it, and how many rods each loaf needed. Finally, the גמרא opens a new topic: an argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about the size of the אמה in the מקדש, which רבי יוחנן says both learn from one פסוק.

steps.title: A covered vessel always follows its covering
steps.stepSummary: The end of ריש לקיש's question, and רבי יוחנן's answer: it makes no difference whether the covering is permanent or not, or whether the rim was covered or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: [ריש לקיש asked: does the rule apply only when one covered] its rim, or even when one did not cover its rim? And רבי יוחנן said to him: Permanent covering or not permanent, rim covered or rim not covered, it makes no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that a wooden vessel covered with metal always takes on the status of its metal covering, with no exceptions. The גמרא is quoting this to build a challenge about the שולחן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beginning of ריש לקיש's question is in the text just before this. רבי יוחנן's broad answer means a gold-covered wooden vessel counts as a gold vessel. If so, the gold-covered שולחן should be a metal vessel that can become טמא anyway, so why did we need a special source for its טומאה?

keyTerms.meaning: Its rim (the raised edge around the vessel)
He covered (with a metal layer)
A permanent, fixed covering
It makes no difference

phrases.aramaic: לְבִזְבְּזָיו, אוֹ בְּשֶׁלֹּא חִיפָּה אֶת לְבִזְבְּזָיו?
phrases.english: its rim, or even where he did not cover its rim?
And he said to him:
There is no difference with a permanent covering,
and no difference with a covering that is not permanent;
no difference if he covered its rim,
and no difference if he did not cover its rim.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר לֵיהּ: לָא שְׁנָא צִיפּוּי עוֹמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question begun before this section and supplies the rule that drives the challenge about the שולחן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Any metal covering, permanent or not, rim covered or not, gives the vessel the status of its covering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A covered vessel follows its covering in every case.

steps.title: Maybe acacia wood is too important to be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the valuable עצי שיטים of the שולחן keep their wooden status. It shows this works for ריש לקיש but not for רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that acacia wood is important and is not cancelled by the covering, that works for ריש לקיש. He said the rule applies only to vessels of אכסלגוס wood from overseas, but vessels of מסמס wood are important and are not cancelled. That works well. But according to רבי יוחנן, who said that even מסמס vessels are cancelled, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a way out: perhaps the שולחן's wood is so valuable that the gold does not cancel it. It then shows that this way out fails according to רבי יוחנן, so the challenge stays strong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש holds that the covering rule applies only to mid-grade wood (אכסלגוס), not to precious wood (מסמס). On his view, valuable עצי שיטים would stay wood. רבי יוחנן holds that even precious wood is cancelled by a covering, so for him the question about the שולחן still needs an answer. The next step gives it.

keyTerms.meaning: Acacia wood, the wood the שולחן was made from
They are important and are not cancelled
A mid-grade type of wood brought from overseas
An expensive, precious type of wood
That works out fine (for one opinion)
What can be said? (the problem remains)

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש are arguing about precious wood. That is a separate point from step 1, where ריש לקיש only asked a question and רבי יוחנן ruled that the covering rule applies broadly.

phrases.english: And if you would say: acacia wood
is important and is not cancelled,
phrases.notes: He means the gold covering does not erase its status as wood.

phrases.english: that works well for ריש לקיש, who said:
They taught it only regarding vessels of akhsalgos wood
which come from overseas,
but vessels of masmas wood are important
and are not cancelled. That works well.
But according to רבי יוחנן, who said:
masmas vessels are also cancelled,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, עֲצֵי שִׁיטִּים חֲשִׁיבִי וְלָא בָּטְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises and rejects a possible defense, which keeps the challenge from step 1 alive.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a special source showing the שולחן is a wooden vessel that can become טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי יוחנן, even precious wood is cancelled by its covering. So the gold-covered שולחן should count as a gold vessel, and the 'important wood' defense fails.

steps.title: The פסוק calls the שולחן wood
steps.stepSummary: The שולחן is different because the פסוק in יחזקאל calls it 'עץ', so it keeps the status of a wooden vessel despite its gold covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שולחן is different, because the Merciful One calls it 'wood'. As it says: 'The altar was of wood, three cubits high, and its length two cubits, and it had corners; and its length and its walls were of wood. And he said to me: This is the table that is before ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: a פסוק describes the שולחן as wood, so it is treated as a wooden vessel even though it was covered in gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule says a covered vessel follows its covering. The שולחן is a special exception because the פסוק itself labels it 'wood'. It is still a vessel; the פסוק only fixes which rules of vessels apply to it. That is why we need the special source about how it becomes טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different (a special case)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳
Wood
The Table on which the לחם הפנים was placed

steps.whatToRemember: The gold-covered שולחן keeps the status of a wooden vessel because the פסוק calls it 'עץ'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the שולחן needs its own special source for טומאה instead of simply counting as a gold vessel.

phrases.english: The Table is different, because the Merciful One called it 'wood',
as it is stated: 'The altar was of wood, three cubits high,'
its length two cubits, and it had its corners,
and its length and its walls were of wood;

phrases.aramaic: וַיְדַבֵּר אֵלַי זֶה הַשֻּׁלְחָן אֲשֶׁר לִפְנֵי ה׳״.
phrases.english: and he said to me: This is the table that is before the Lord.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question left open in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural exception: the פסוק defines the שולחן as wood.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The gold-covered שולחן should count as a gold vessel under רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק calls it wood, so it keeps the status of a wooden vessel.

steps.title: Why does the verse switch from altar to table?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק opens by calling the object a 'מזבח' and closes by calling it a 'שולחן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It began with 'altar' and ended with 'table'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices something odd in the פסוק it just quoted and asks about it. This sets up the teaching in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both words in the פסוק describe the same object, so the change of name needs an explanation. The question is about how to read the פסוק, not about the טומאה discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: He opened, began
He finished, concluded
Altar

phrases.english: It began with 'altar' and concluded with 'table'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Branches off from the פסוק quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the same object is called both 'מזבח' and 'שולחן' in one פסוק.

steps.title: Today a person's table brings atonement
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר explain that when the בית המקדש stood, the מזבח brought כפרה; now a person's table brings כפרה for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both say: When the בית המקדש stands, the altar atones for a person. Now that the בית המקדש is not standing, a person's table atones for him.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question: the פסוק moves from 'altar' to 'table' to teach that, without the בית המקדש, a person's table takes over the מזבח's role of bringing כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change of wording becomes a lesson. The table here means a person's own dinner table, used for kindness such as feeding guests and the poor. Today it does what the מזבח used to do.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
The Temple is standing
Atones, brings forgiveness

steps.whatToRemember: Today, a person's table brings כפרה, the way the מזבח did when the בית המקדש stood.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous lesson about how a person can earn כפרה today, through generosity at his own table.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar both say:
When the Temple is standing,
the altar atones for a person;
and now that the Temple is not standing,
a person's table atones for him.
phrases.notes: The idea is a table used to feed guests and the poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק moves from מזבח to שולחן to teach that today a person's table brings כפרה in place of the מזבח.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Without the בית המקדש, a person's table takes the place of the מזבח in bringing כפרה.

steps.title: Where do we learn the gold panels of the Table?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about four gold panels on the שולחן and asks what the Torah source for this is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said there were four gold panels there. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה about the four gold panels on the שולחן and asks for its source in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה described the parts of the שולחן: gold panels standing at its sides, with rods resting on them to hold the loaves of לחם הפנים. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows these parts come from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Panels or posts. Here, the four gold uprights at the sides of the שולחן.
"From where are these matters?" A request for a source, usually a פסוק.
The Table in the מקדש that held the לחם הפנים.

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעָה סְנִיפִין שֶׁל זָהָב הָיוּ שָׁם [וְכוּ׳].
phrases.english: There were four panels of gold there, etc.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It moves from the כפרה teaching about the table to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the gold panels (and the rods) of the שולחן.

steps.title: A verse lists the molds, bowls, panels and rods
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא quotes the פסוק in שמות about the שולחן's vessels. He explains each word as one part: molds, frankincense bowls, panels, and rods that cover the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said: the פסוק says, "You shall make its dishes, its pans, its קשותיו and its מנקיותיו." The dishes are the bread molds. The pans are the frankincense bowls. The קשותיו are the panels. The מנקיותיו are the rods. "With which it shall be covered" means the rods cover the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: רב קטינא answers the question. He reads four words in one פסוק as four parts of the שולחן, and the panels and rods are among them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hard words in the פסוק, קשותיו and מנקיותיו, become the panels and the rods. The ending, "אשר יסך בהן", tells us what the rods are for: they sit over the loaves like a cover. This makes the rods sound like a Torah-level requirement, and that sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: "Its dishes." Explained as the molds for the bread.
Molds used to shape the loaves of לחם הפנים.
Bowls holding the frankincense (לבונה) placed with the bread.
Rods that rest on the panels and hold up the loaves.
Covering. The rods are laid over the bread.

steps.whyThisMatters: Once the rods come from a פסוק, it looks like they are required by the Torah. That is exactly what רבא challenges next.

phrases.english: Rav Ketina said: The verse states:
"And you shall make its dishes and its pans,
and its kesot and its menakiyot."
"Its dishes" – these are the molds.
"Its pans" – these are the bowls,
phrases.notes: These are the bowls for the frankincense that sits on the table with the bread.

phrases.english: "Its kesot" – these are the panels.
"And its menakiyot" – these are the rods.
"With which it shall be covered" –
that the bread is covered with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in שמות 25:29 lists the parts: dishes are molds, pans are bowls, קשותיו are panels, מנקיותיו are rods that cover the bread.

steps.title: If the rods are from the Torah, why don't they override Shabbat?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the idea that the rods are from the Torah. A משנה says arranging and removing them does not override שבת, but Torah-required services in the מקדש normally do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: we learned that arranging the rods and removing them do not override שבת. If you think the rods are from the Torah, why don't they override שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב קטינא's reading. He uses a משנה that says the rods are not handled on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Torah-required service in the מקדש is normally allowed even on שבת. So if the rods are דאורייתא, setting them up should be allowed on שבת too. The משנה forbids it, which suggests the rods are only a later, rabbinic addition.

keyTerms.meaning: Overrides שבת. The action is allowed even though it is normally forbidden labor.
Arranging. Here, putting the rods in place.
Removing. Here, taking the rods out.
From the Torah itself, as opposed to rabbinic law.
"If it enters your mind." Used to show a thought leads to a problem.

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
Neither the arranging of the rods nor their removal
overrides Shabbat.
And if it enters your mind that they are required by Torah law,
why do they not override Shabbat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea from step 7 that the rods are a Torah requirement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב קטינא's reading that the rods (מנקיותיו) come from the Torah.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Torah-required services in the מקדש override שבת. The משנה says handling the rods does not, so the rods would seem not to be from the Torah.

steps.title: רבא takes back his challenge
steps.stepSummary: רבא retracts his objection. Based on רבי עקיבא's rule, anything that could be done before שבת does not override שבת, and handling the rods can be arranged around שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then said: what I said is not right. We learned a rule from רבי עקיבא: any work that can be done before שבת does not override שבת. These rods can also be handled in a way that does not need to override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down his own question. The rods not overriding שבת does not prove they are rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even Torah-required work only overrides שבת when it cannot be done some other way. The rods can be removed before שבת and set up after שבת, so there is no need to break שבת for them. רב קטינא's source stands.

keyTerms.meaning: "What I said is nothing." A sage taking back his own statement.
A general rule.
Labor that is forbidden on שבת.
It can be done before שבת begins.

steps.whatToRemember: Being from the Torah is not enough to override שבת. If the job can be done before or after שבת, it does not override שבת. So the rods can still be דאורייתא.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that the rods are rabbinic because they don't override שבת. רבא's final view is that this proves nothing, since the work could be done at another time.
steps.whyThisMatters: This uses רבי עקיבא's general rule for when Torah-required work overrides שבת. The rule applies far beyond the rods.

phrases.english: Rava then said:
What I said is not correct,
as we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Akiva stated a principle:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מְלָאכָה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לָהּ לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת –
phrases.english: Any labor that can be done on the eve of Shabbat
does not override Shabbat.
And with these too, it is possible
that Shabbat need not be overridden for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רָבָא: לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא דַּאֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא answers his own challenge from step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof in step 8 that the rods are not from the Torah.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not overriding שבת can come from רבי עקיבא's rule, since the work could be done at another time. It does not show the rods are rabbinic.

steps.title: The rods are only there to stop mold, so they can wait
steps.stepSummary: The rods keep the bread from getting moldy. A short gap of time over שבת will not make it moldy, so the rods can be handled before and after שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are the rods needed? So the bread does not get moldy. In such a short amount of time, it will not get moldy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why the rods do not need to be handled on שבת itself. Their only job is to prevent mold, and a short delay will not cause mold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up רבא's retraction in Step 9: the rods can still be a Torah requirement. Their only purpose is to keep the bread from getting moldy, and that purpose is not harmed if they are missing for a short time. That is why taking them out and putting them back can be done before or after שבת, so it does not push aside שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason
to become moldy
an amount or measure (here, of time)
the rods placed between the loaves

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking why the rods are needed in the first place.

phrases.english: So that the bread should not get moldy;
in such a short amount of time it does not get moldy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the rods can be arranged around שבת, which supports רבא's retraction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the purpose of the rods
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a Torah-required service with the rods must be done on time, even on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the rods only prevent mold, and a short delay causes no mold, the work can wait until after שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא describes removing and replacing the rods
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the procedure. The כהן removes the rods on ערב שבת and lays them along the table. On מוצאי שבת he lifts each loaf and slides a rod back under it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: How is it done? He goes in on ערב שבת, slides the rods out, and lays them along the length of the table. After שבת he goes in, lifts the ends of a loaf, and puts a rod under it. Then he lifts the ends of the next loaf and puts a rod under it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the rods really were taken out before שבת and put back after שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is support for the point just made. The rods are removed on Friday, so the new bread sits without them over שבת. They go back in only on מוצאי שבת. So in practice no rod work was ever done on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Friday, before שבת begins
slides them out
after שבת ends (Saturday night)
a loaf (of the לחם הפנים)
a rod

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: How is it done?
He goes in on ערב שבת and slides them out,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the rods between the loaves.

phrases.english: and lays them along the length of the table.
And after שבת ends, he goes in,
lifts the ends of a loaf
and puts a rod under it,
and again lifts the ends of a loaf
and puts a rod under it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the claim that the rods are handled before and after שבת.
steps.raayaObject: That rod handling is arranged around שבת, not done on it
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing removal on ערב שבת and reinsertion on מוצאי שבת

steps.title: How many rods each loaf needs
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Each of the four middle loaves needs three rods. The top loaf needs only two. The bottom loaf needs none, because it sits right on the table.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four loaves need three rods each. The top loaf needs only two, because nothing presses down on it. The bottom loaf needs none at all, because it rests on the table's surface itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on to list exactly how many rods each loaf in a stack of six needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each stack has six loaves. The four middle loaves carry weight from above, so each one gets three rods. The top loaf has nothing on it, so two rods are enough. The bottom loaf sits on the table itself, so it needs no rods.

keyTerms.meaning: the top loaf
the bottom loaf
weight, a load
the table's own surface

steps.whatToRemember: The rods are a real part of the שולחן, but they only prevent mold. So they are removed before שבת and put back after שבת, and they never push aside שבת.

phrases.english: Four loaves need
phrases.notes: These are the four middle loaves in each stack of six.

phrases.english: three rods each;
the top one needs only two,
because there is no weight on it;
the bottom one needs none at all,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁמּוּנַּחַת עַל טׇהֳרוֹ שֶׁל שׁוּלְחָן.
phrases.english: because it rests on the surface of the table itself.
phrases.notes: טהרו literally means "its purity." Here it means the bare surface of the table.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְבָּעָה חַלּוֹת צְרִיכוֹת שְׁלֹשָׁה שְׁלֹשָׁה קָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the details of the rods.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Middle loaves get three rods each, the top loaf gets two, and the bottom loaf gets none.

steps.title: How big was an אמה in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins with a משנה in כלים. רבי מאיר says all the אמות in the מקדש were medium-sized, except for a few altar measurements. רבי יהודה says a building אמה was six handbreadths and a vessel אמה was five.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: רבי מאיר says that all the אמות used in the מקדש were medium אמות, except for the golden altar, the corner, the surrounding ledge, and the base. רבי יהודה says that the אמה for building was six handbreadths, and the one for vessels was five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion by quoting a משנה about the size of the אמה used in the מקדש. This sets up the analysis that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says one standard medium אמה was used everywhere, with a short list of altar exceptions. רבי יהודה splits it differently: buildings used a six-handbreadth אמה, while vessels like the שולחן used a smaller five-handbreadth אמה. This matters for the שולחן, which is a vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: cubits (units of length)
medium-sized

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. רבי מאיר makes his exceptions by specific altar parts. רבי יהודה makes his split by category: buildings versus vessels.

phrases.english: We learned in a משנה elsewhere:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in כלים 17:10.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
all the cubits that were in the Temple were medium ones,
phrases.notes: A "medium" אמה here means six handbreadths. The exceptions that follow used a smaller one.

and the corner, the surrounding ledge, and the base.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
the cubit for building is six handbreadths,
and the one for vessels is five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about measurements in the מקדש, now that the discussion of the rods is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: all מקדש אמות were medium, except certain altar parts. רבי יהודה: a building אמה is six handbreadths and a vessel אמה is five.
steps.whyThisMatters: The size of the אמה decides the real dimensions of the שולחן and the other vessels, which the גמרא will go on to discuss.

steps.title: Both opinions come from one verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה both base their opinions on the same פסוק: 'And these are the measures of the מזבח by cubits: a cubit is a cubit and a handbreadth.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both of them learned their opinions from one פסוק: 'And these are the measures of the altar by cubits: the cubit is a cubit and a handbreadth.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן tells us where the argument about the size of the אמה comes from. This sets up the next part, where the גמרא will show how each side reads the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we only had the two opinions from the משנה in כלים. Now we learn they are not arguing from different sources. They are reading the same words differently. The key phrase is 'a cubit and a handbreadth,' which suggests there is more than one size of אמה.

keyTerms.meaning: One פסוק. Both sages use the same verse.
They expounded, meaning they learned a law from the words of the פסוק.
The measurements of the altar.
A cubit, a unit of length made of a set number of handbreadths.
A handbreadth, roughly the width of four fingers.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think one sage has a פסוק and the other does not. רבי יוחנן's point is that both use the very same פסוק and simply read it differently.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
And both of them expounded one verse:
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה from the משנה in כלים.
